subject: Progressive release: temporary SLA carve-out request for NovaCorp
messages:
From: Natalie Chen <natalie.chen@novacorp.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Prod cutover and SLA during staged release

Hi Rafael / Marissa,

We have a narrow production cutover window for the smart-search feature (targeting 11/09). Our SRE team is concerned about the impact of a progressive rollout on the 99.9% uptime SLA during the first 48 hours when we ramp traffic. Can Redwood provide a documented mitigation (policy/config) that allows us to:

- run a gradual traffic ramp (0 -> 5% -> 20% -> 60% -> 100%) over 48h,
- pin to a stable model variant automatically if p95 latency exceeds threshold, and
- accept a temporary, explicit SLA adjustment for the ramp window if needed?

We attached a short SOC2 brief and our network requirements spreadsheet for reference. Please let me know what product/runtime controls you'll apply and whether Redwood needs a separate deployment (dedicated pool) to avoid SLA risk.

Thanks,
Natalie Chen
Director, Platform Engineering
NovaCorp

Attachments: SOC2-brief.pdf, network-reqs.xlsx
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Natalie Chen <natalie.chen@novacorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Prod cutover and SLA during staged release

Hi Natalie — appreciate the heads up and the attachments. Short answer: yes, we can support a progressive release with explicit mitigations; need a quick alignment on thresholds and operational handoffs. Proposed approach below (high level):

1) Progressive traffic plan (we mirror your ramp): 0% -> 5% (1h) -> 20% (6h) -> 60% (24h) -> 100% (remaining).

2) Automated safety controls we will enable for NovaCorp during the ramp:
   - Latency trip: if p95 increases by >40% vs baseline for a 10m sliding window, we auto-pin traffic back to the prior stable model variant and route all new requests there for 30 minutes while we investigate.
   - Error spike: if 5xx rate >0.5% for 5m, immediate rollback to pinned variant and page SRE on-call.
   - Gradual manual override: customer can pause or accelerate ramp from Console or via API key-scoped route.

3) Temporary SLA carve-out: we can commit to a documented carve-out for the 48h ramp window where the uptime SLA is adjusted to 99.5% for the affected route. Outside the window standard SLA applies. We will reflect this in a short addendum (DPA rider) for sign-off.

4) Observability & runbooks: we will attach the mitigation config (proposed-mitigation-cfg.yaml) to the customer account, enable traffic-level tracing and a 30s latency dashboard alert for the route.

5) Deployment option: unless you require strict isolation, this can be achieved on Hosted with autoscaling + pin/fallback. If you'd prefer guaranteed capacity, we can propose a Dedicated pool quote (separate SLA).

Next steps:
- If that approach sounds OK, Marissa can kick off a short DPA addendum and liaise with your procurement.
- Laura / Runtime: can you confirm the default auto-pin window (30m) and whether we should extend to 60m for models with cold KV caches?

Rafael
VP, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed-mitigation-cfg.yaml (draft)
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T13:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Prod cutover and SLA during staged release

Rafael / team —

Thanks for the proposed controls. A few clarifying points from Product/Runtime before we ship the addendum:

- Baseline definition: we should base the p95 baseline on the 7-day rolling median for the same route and sequence-length distribution. Document that in the addendum.
- Auto-pin behavior: 30m is OK for warm models; for models with large KV state we should default to 60m to avoid oscillation. Suggest we make the window configurable per-account.
- Canary duration per step: tightening the 5% -> 20% jump to include health-check gates (no 5xx >0.1% for 30m) before increasing.
- Monitoring: enable prefix/KV cache metrics and a Canary dashboard template (we'll share the Drive runbook link).

I'll attach a quick YAML stub for the mitigation and we'll surface the exact SLO language for the DPA. If Procurement needs the Dedicated quote, Marissa please prepare the 30-day estimate.

Laura Bennett
Head of Product, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Rafael / team — thanks, that all seems reasonable. One small ask from Procurement / Legal: can the DPA addendum explicitly call out the 48-hour ramp window and the temporary 99.5% uptime for that route, with the automatic-pin and rollback rules included as operational controls? Our SRE also prefers the 60m pin window for the initial rollout to avoid cache thrash.

If you send the addendum and the mitigation YAML I'll route to Legal and Procurement today. We'll aim to sign before Nov 6 to keep the 11/9 cutover.

Best,
Natalie

NovaCorp
